tool.help:
**What this tool does**
**Focaloop ExpressionLoop** measures differential gene and isoform expression from RNA-seq data without downloading or aligning 100% of every sequencing archive. It works with either FASTQ files already in your Galaxy History or public SRA/ENA run accessions streamed on demand.
-----
**How it works**
1. **Transcriptome preparation:** Builds spliced transcript sequences from your reference FASTA and GTF/GFF3 annotation (plus non-coding background decoys to trap intronic or intergenic reads). When a secondary assembly, strain, or co-infecting pathogen is supplied, both references are indexed together and homologous genes are linked automatically. 2. **Pilot aligner check:** Samples a small slice of reads from the first run (default 25,000 reads) and benchmarks installed aligners on real mapping rate, paralog tie handling, and simulated control reads to select the best aligner for your transcriptome. 3. **Balanced wave streaming:** Reads data in growing waves, directing more reads to shallower libraries so replicate depths stay balanced. Ambiguous reads shared across isoforms, paralogs, or secondary assemblies are resolved with expectation-maximization, and placement uncertainty is propagated into the differential expression test. 4. **Adaptive stopping:** After each wave, ExpressionLoop checks whether every sample has passed a safe minimum mapped depth, whether gene fold changes have stopped shifting between waves, and whether technical sequencing noise is small compared to biological variation across replicates. Once those criteria pass (or the reading budget cap is reached), streaming stops. 5. **Borderline-gene refinement and state export:** Optionally scans one final slice of reads through a fast k-mer filter to add evidence for borderline or low-count genes while skipping already-saturated abundant transcripts. Results are exported alongside a compact `.focaloop.tar.zst` state bundle.
**Local Galaxy History files vs. Logan unitigs vs. raw SRA/ENA streaming**
- **Galaxy History FASTQ files:** Under the default **Automatic** budget, ExpressionLoop processes up to 100% of your local files (stopping earlier only if fold-change and variance criteria already converged cleanly), so small local datasets are never truncated prematurely. - **Public SRA/ENA accessions with Logan unitigs (default for remote manifests):** When every run in your manifest is available in the public Logan archive, ExpressionLoop streams compact pre-assembled 31-mer unitigs (~15-35x smaller than raw FASTQ archives), resolves multi-mapping genes with operon-aware expectation-maximization, scales k-mer abundance to expected fragment counts using ENA read lengths, and runs differential expression directly. - **Raw public SRA/ENA partial-file streaming:** When Logan is turned off or any run is not yet in Logan, ExpressionLoop falls back uniformly across all samples to partial-file streaming over the network and stops as soon as the contrast stabilizes (capped at 12% of each archive unless you pick a higher budget preset).
**What is saved in the state bundle**
The `.focaloop.tar.zst` archive stores the transcript catalog, per-sample gene and transcript counts, placement uncertainty estimates, sample metadata, a small held-out read slice for independent validation, and a statistical test ledger. Pass this bundle directly to **Focaloop Query** to test additional group comparisons or alternative model formulas in seconds without re-reading any FASTQ files.
-----
**Choosing an input mode**
| Your data | Input mode to choose | What you provide | |---|---|---| | Paired-end FASTQs in your Galaxy History | **Galaxy History paired-end collection (list:paired)** | A `list:paired` collection plus a sample sheet TSV matching collection IDs | | Single-end FASTQs in your Galaxy History | **Galaxy History single-end FASTQ files** | Selected FASTQ(.gz) datasets plus a sample sheet TSV matching dataset names | | Public SRA/ENA runs or remote HTTPS FASTQs | **Public SRA/ENA accessions or remote FASTQ URLs** | Either upload a TSV/CSV manifest or type condition groups and run accessions directly into the inline builder |
-----
**Inputs and manifest format**
Choose your primary reference genome and matching gene annotation using one of three sources:
- **Built-in Galaxy genome (CVMFS cache, default):** Pick a genome pre-cached on this Galaxy server. By default ExpressionLoop fetches and verifies the matching RefSeq gene annotation automatically (UCSC RefSeq GTF for standard builds, or contig-normalized NCBI RefSeq GFF3 for microbes and non-UCSC builds) and rejects mismatched contig lengths instead of silently shifting coordinates. You can override this with a GTF or GFF3 file from your History at any time. - **Genome and annotation from your Galaxy History:** Select your own reference genome FASTA and GTF or GFF3 file (`.gz` supported). - **Fetch automatically by NCBI assembly accession:** Enter a RefSeq (`GCF_` prefix, recommended because it provides curated gene annotation) or GenBank (`GCA_` prefix) assembly accession to download both the genome FASTA and its matching NCBI GFF3 automatically, with an optional History GTF/GFF3 override.
Optionally expand **Additional reference genomes and multi-strain pan-transcriptome** to include extra assemblies in two ways:
- **Explicit additional reference genomes:** Add any number of extra strains, older annotation releases, plasmids, or co-infecting pathogens (each chosen from NCBI accession, built-in CVMFS cache with automatic RefSeq annotation or History GTF/GFF3, or your History). - **Automatic related RefSeq strain expansion (opt-in):** Automatically discover and fetch up to *K* strain-deduplicated RefSeq genomes with gene annotations for the same species on NCBI (inferred automatically from a built-in CVMFS genome or primary NCBI accession, or specified by species name or taxonomy ID for History genomes) to capture accessory genes absent from your primary assembly.
Your sample sheet or manifest must be a tab-separated (TSV) or comma-separated (CSV) file with a header row:
| Column | Required | Description | |---|---|---| | `sample_id` | Yes | Unique sample name (must match collection or dataset identifiers for History inputs) | | `condition` | Yes | Experimental group name referenced by your contrast and model formula | | `run_or_url` | Remote mode | Public SRA/ENA run accession (`SRR`, `ERR`, or `DRR` prefix) or HTTPS FASTQ URL | | `mate2_url` | Remote paired FASTQ | Second mate URL for remote paired-end FASTQ links | | `layout` | Optional | `PE` (paired-end) or `SE` (single-end), auto-detected when omitted | | `batch` (or any extra column) | Optional | Covariate column used in your model formula (for example, `~batch + condition`) |
Example sample sheet for Galaxy History FASTQ files:
``` sample_id condition batch ctrl_1 control batch_1 ctrl_2 control batch_2 trt_1 treated batch_1 trt_2 treated batch_2 ```
Example manifest for public accessions or remote URLs:
``` sample_id condition batch run_or_url ctrl_1 control batch_1 RUN_ACCESSION_1 ctrl_2 control batch_2 RUN_ACCESSION_2 trt_1 treated batch_1 https://example.org/reads/trt_1.fastq.gz trt_2 treated batch_2 https://example.org/reads/trt_2.fastq.gz ```
-----
**Key parameters**
- **Primary differential expression contrast (`--contrast`):** Written as `factor:groupA:groupB` (for example, `condition:treated:control`). Positive `log2FoldChange` means higher expression in `groupA`. - **Statistical model formula (`--design`):** Default `~condition`. Add covariates from your sample sheet to control for batch or donor effects (for example, `~batch + condition`). - **Data reading budget:** Leave on **Automatic** for routine work. Choose **Adaptive high-precision (30%)** or **Uncapped adaptive (up to 100%)** when you want higher depth for rare isoforms or low-abundance transcripts on remote archives. - **Extra pass for borderline and low-count genes:** Enabled by default. Gathers extra counts for genes near the significance boundary without spending alignment time on saturated housekeeping genes.
-----
**Outputs**
1. **Differential expression table (`de_results.tsv`):** Gene-level differential expression results sorted by adjusted p-value (`padj`). 2. **HTML report:** Self-contained visual summary showing aligner benchmark scores, fraction of each file read vs. skipped, wave convergence plots, a volcano plot, and top differentially expressed genes. 3. **State bundle (`expression_state.focaloop.tar.zst`):** Compact saved state ready for instant follow-up contrasts in **Focaloop Query**. 4. **Transcript abundances (`transcript_abundances.tsv`, optional):** Enabled under **Additional outputs**. Reports per-sample effective transcript counts, TPM, and within-gene isoform proportion (`isoform_fraction_psi`).
Key columns in `de_results.tsv`:
| Column | Meaning | |---|---| | `gene_id`, `gene_name` | Gene identifier and symbol from your primary annotation | | `ortholog_bridge` | Linked gene ID(s) in the secondary assembly when dual-reference mode is enabled | | `baseMean` | Mean normalized count across all samples | | `log2FoldChange` | Estimated log2 fold change (`groupA` relative to `groupB`) | | `lfcSE_deseq2`, `lfcSE_total` | Standard error from replicate counts alone, and total standard error including multi-mapping uncertainty | | `ci95_low`, `ci95_high` | 95% confidence interval for `log2FoldChange` | | `pvalue`, `padj` | Raw p-value and Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value (FDR) | | `placement_var_frac`, `tech_var_frac` | Fraction of variance from multi-mapping ambiguity and from total technical sequencing noise | | `streamed_reads` | Total reads assigned to this gene across the study | | `zoomed`, `status` | Whether the gene received extra borderline-scan reads and its final call status |
-----
**Tips and troubleshooting**
- **Contrast level not found:** Check that the factor name and both group labels in `--contrast` match exact values in your sample sheet (including capitalization). - **Sample names not matching History inputs:** Ensure `sample_id` matches each element identifier in your `list:paired` collection or the base name of each single-end FASTQ dataset. - **Testing more group comparisons later:** Do not re-run ExpressionLoop from scratch. Pass the saved **State bundle (.focaloop.tar.zst)** to **Focaloop Query** to test additional contrasts immediately. - **Public archive access restricted on your cluster:** Switch **Remote archive transport** to **ENA HTTPS partial-file streaming** or upload FASTQ datasets to your Galaxy History first.
